dialect.detail: IBM mainframe batch COBOL; uses RECORDING MODE IS F, BLOCK CONTAINS 0 RECORDS, LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD, GOBACK, COMP index, JCL DD names (EMPROJ, SYSOUT), and dataset naming conventions (RTPOT44.LEARN.EMP1.PROJ) typical of IBM z/OS environment

purpose.domain_detail: COBOL table/array processing exercise using an employee project file; authored by Doretha Riley in 2020
purpose.summary: This program reads an employee project file into a table (array) of up to 20 entries, then performs searches and calculations: finding employees on project A111, finding NC programmer/analysts eligible for overtime billing, computing total cost for project A111, and computing total cost across all projects. It is a structured learning exercise demonstrating COBOL table handling with OCCURS, INDEXED BY, and PERFORM VARYING.

notable_features: OCCURS 20 TIMES with ASCENDING KEY IS and INDEXED BY
PERFORM VARYING with index and subscript
Inline DISPLAY of table entries during load
No SEARCH/SEARCH ALL used despite ASCENDING KEY defined — manual PERFORM VARYING used instead
High comment ratio (60%) with structured paragraph documentation blocks
verdict.notes: Source is truncated at 16000 chars but all four divisions and main logic are visible. The program is clearly a student/tutorial exercise authored in 2020 for an IBM mainframe COBOL course. No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS. No COPY statements. Comment ratio of 60% is consistent with instructional code with heavy documentation requirements.
